ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio — Frontline is not an ADS program representing multiple ordinary shares: the NYSE-traded security is the ordinary share itself, so per-ordinary-share figures are directly comparable to the traded FRO price with no scaling.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-27, SEC EDGAR https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/913290/000162828026021774/fro-20251231.htm), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'Ordinary Shares, Nominal Value $1.00 Per Share', trading symbol FRO, listed on the New York Stock Exchange — the NYSE security is the ordinary share itself (also listed on the Oslo Stock Exchange under the same symbol), not an ADS

moat_against: Pure spot price taker — TCE rates are set by the market for a fungible vessel; no pricing power, no customer lock-in, deliberate spot exposure
Returns are the cycle, not a franchise: roic_proxy -5.82% FY2017 and 0.25% FY2021 vs 13.76% FY2023 (fundamentals.json); operating margin 1.9% FY2021 vs 40.9% FY2023 on spot rates alone

The fleet is wasting capital: replacement capex is huge and lumpy — $1,631.4M in FY2023 and $915.2M in FY2024 (financials_history.csv) — and nine VLCC newbuilding contracts were agreed in 2026 for $1,224.0M with $601.1M of commitments remaining at Q2 2026 (search-cited)
Leverage amplifies the cycle: net debt $2,816.4M at FY2025 (dcf_numbers.json) against a normalized owner's-earnings base that is negative
The dividend is a pass-through of spot earnings, not a through-cycle return — it was zero in FY2021 (fundamentals.json dividend notes)
moat_for: Scale: largest publicly listed pure-play tanker owner after the October 2023 purchase of 24 VLCCs from Euronav, which took the fleet from 65 to 89 vessels (search-cited company release)

Modern ECO fleet with a large scrubber-fitted share and low vessel operating costs (Q2 2026 fleetwide opex about $8,700/day excluding dry-docking, search-cited company release) — a low cash breakeven through troughs
Counter-cyclical fleet trading and capital access: anchor shareholder Hemen/Fredriksen, and older VLCCs sold into the strong 2026 market (search-cited)
moat_justification: A spot tanker owner is a pure price taker: charterers pay the market time-charter-equivalent rate for a fungible vessel, there are no switching costs, no network effects and no pricing power — Frontline deliberately runs mostly spot exposure, so its earnings are the tanker cycle, not a franchise. The return history proves it: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json was -5.82% in FY2017 and 0.25% in FY2021, then 10.13% / 13.76% / 13.57% / 11.06% in FY2022-FY2025 as spot rates spiked — above the cost of capital only in upcycle years. Gross margin is not separately tagged in its IFRS filings (fundamentals.json carries it as null), so operating margin is the margin evidence: 1.9% in FY2021, 31.0% in FY2022, 40.9% in FY2023, 36.1% in FY2024, 30.4% in FY2025 — a rate series, not a margin structure. What keeps the score at 3 rather than 0-2 is real but non-durable advantage: scale as the largest publicly listed pure-play tanker owner after the 2023 Euronav fleet purchase, a modern ECO/scrubber fleet with low daily operating costs, disciplined counter-cyclical fleet trading, and an anchor shareholder with deep access to capital. None of that sets the price of its product.
name: Frontline plc
one_liner: Spot tanker price-taker, moat 3/10 — Tier F: no positive normalized owner's earnings (3-yr median OE/share -$0.79; OE positive in only 2 of the last 5 years) because Euronav-era fleet capex swamps operating cash flow in the median window, so the OE DCF produces no IV and no price clears a 15% hurdle on normalized numbers; the $52.49 price is a bet on the 2026 spot-rate super-cycle (record Q2 2026 profit, search-cited), not on through-cycle owner's earnings.
